architectReview.evidence: Leader review of src/local/rerun.rs (read in full) + src/server/llm.rs heal_test + main.rs wiring. The critical safety semantic is correct and load-bearing: heal is gated on `heal && verdict == "fragility" && llm.is_some()`; a `bug` or `env` verdict (or heal disabled / no key) falls straight through to a plain FAIL and counts toward the exit code — a real bug can never be turned green. On a successful heal_test the original id is force-preserved before store::add_value (overwrites tests/<id>.json in place), the seam re-runs the healed case ONCE, and `healed` is set only if that re-run actually passes (a still-broken case reports STILL-FAILING, never a false HEALED). All error paths (analyze/heal/store) are best-effort tracing::warn! + treat as un-healed failure, matching run.rs. No slop, no duplication beyond the shared setup, idiomatic Rust (let-chains). Reuses ExecCtx/for_kind/LlmClient — no forked logic.

executorQa.evidence: Two complementary LIVE runs with a real OpenAI key prove the two guarantees. (1) Anti-masking guard (artifacts/heal-e2e.txt): a spec expecting 201 while the app correctly returns 200 was classified `[bug]` by analyze_failure, so `test rerun --heal` REFUSED to heal it — it stayed FAIL, exit 1, and the case on disk was unchanged (a real behavioral discrepancy is never healed into green). (2) Heal-path trigger (executor 6-AutoHeal live smoke): an unreachable target classified `fragility` DID trigger heal_test (it corrected the case), store::add_value overwrote in place (id preserved), the seam re-ran once, and because the target was still unreachable it correctly reported STILL-FAILING (exit 1) — no false HEALED. build clean, clippy 0, cargo test 13/13.
